items.title: Sam Kininger interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 27, 2011
items.q: I got to play with Maceo Parker, Fred Wesley and Pee Wee Ellis, on stage, right next to me.

ctx.x: Was the — I don’t know if I could call it a decision — but you sort of entered this subfield of funk, instrumental funk. Was that — what made you go in that direction as opposed to becoming like more of a bebop player?

Well we kind of touched on it before we started, I am more of a percussive type, a rhythmic player I guess you could say. So I gravitated to people like Maceo Parker and things like that. And I was like, oh, this feels right. And at the same time I could throw in what little jazz stuff that I did have, and incorporate it into the distilling process of you know, jazz is definitely a more complicated situation, where in the jam band world type thing it’s maybe a modal or like a one chord thing. But you can expound…

It does. And it makes me think of well, one of my questions I wanted to ask you. The term jam band, I think I’ve probably heard that, one of the first times I heard it they were referring to the band Pfish.
